title: Coordinated plan execution
description:
Implement `--execute` for `jit archive document` and `jit archive container` as one coordinated operation over the storage mutation primitive and the shared planner. Execution acquires and holds the repository write guard across the whole operation, recomputes the plan from current state (preview output is never an execution input), creates the container directory with its hidden ownership marker naming the container on first use, refuses non-terminal containers and document targets with any non-terminal direct or embedded-closure owner (a managed zero-owner document executes with informational evidence), stages and verifies content identities captured under the guard, validates every supported local edge in the proposed destination layout, publishes atomically with no replacement, applies exactly the planned reference changes while leaving pinned references untouched, refreshes or invalidates cached asset metadata on moved references, and appends one archive event recording publications, reference changes, and planned deletions; an event-append failure reverts the just-applied reference changes, and when both the append and the revert fail, a rerun that detects destination-rooted references uncovered by any recorded archive event appends one reconciling event describing the observed adopted state, so no reference mutation persists permanently unrecorded. Sources are deleted last, each under one unified precondition: every selected reference for the artifact already points at its destination in durable issue state, and the file re-verifies against its recorded SHA-256 and byte size. Failed deletions are reported warnings. Rerunning after any partial failure converges by recomputation: a content-identical occupied destination is adopted as already archived, residual sources are rediscovered through the inverse mirror mapping and removed under the same precondition, and a run that mutates nothing appends no event.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Before metadata commit, every staged supported local edge is validated against the proposed destination layout rather than source-resolved paths.
- [hard] REQ-02: Execution is refused on a non-terminal container and on a document target with any non-terminal direct or embedded-closure owner, while a managed zero-owner document executes with informational evidence.
- [hard] REQ-03: Exactly the planned reference changes are applied — pinned references untouched, container targets relink only unpinned references owned by terminal issues inside the subtree, document targets relink every unpinned direct owner, unselected references remain source-resolvable — and one write guard is held from recomputation through the final deletion attempt.
- [hard] REQ-04: One archive event is appended by every mutating execution — publication-only executions included — after publications and reference changes persist and before deletions, recording publications, reference changes, and planned deletions; an event-append failure reverts the just-applied reference changes; a rerun that mutates nothing appends no event, except that adopted state uncovered by any recorded archive event (destination-rooted references or already-archived mirror content) triggers one reconciling event; event append performs tail repair so a torn trailing record stays one isolated line, and archive-path event reading skips it.
- [hard] REQ-05: A source is deleted only when every selected reference for its artifact already points at the destination in durable issue state and the file matches its recorded content identity; a mismatch or unrelinked reference skips the deletion with a reported warning and the file stays.
- [hard] REQ-06: Failure injection for partial staging (including staged-temp cleanup verification), partial relink, event-append failure with and without a successful compensating revert, deletion failure, and a source edited after planning proves no artifact is lost, no destination overwritten, and no reference relying solely on a missing path; a rerun after each injected failure reaches a stable, fully reported state with already-archived adoption, inverse-mapping residue rediscovery, and no duplicate destination, reference, or event, where an identity-mismatched edited source is retained indefinitely with its warning as the correct terminal outcome.
